title: Dismissal policy: dismiss-permanently, dismiss-until-next-major and dismiss-until-next-minor each have a defined runtime clause
description: The completion store honours the elicited dismissal-policy with a runtime clause per option. `dismiss-permanently` writes a terminal completion record and refuses re-surfacing regardless of any subsequent version bump: a principal who dismisses the tour never sees it again until the restart-tour control fires. `dismiss-until-next-major` writes a completion record carrying the current tour version and compares stored and current versions on the major segment on principal load: the tour re-surfaces when the majors differ, otherwise it stays dismissed. `dismiss-until-next-minor` writes a completion record carrying the current tour version and re-surfaces the tour when either the major or the minor segment differs on principal load. The record shape is identical across the three policies; only the comparison on load differs.
rationale: The elicit offers three dismissal policies but no requirement described what each option does. A principal on a project that chose `dismiss-until-next-major` inherited `dismiss-permanently` behaviour silently. Requiring a per-option clause turns the elicit into a chain-linked behaviour the completion store's read on load proves.
